tagline: Iterates row-by-row, evaluates an expression, then sums all results

slides.title: How SUMX Works
slides.body: SUMX takes a table and an expression. It visits every row of the table, evaluates the expression in that row's context, and finally sums all the row-level results.
slides.keyPoint: SUMX(Table, Expression) — think of it as a for-loop that calculates something per row, then adds everything up.

slides.title: Orders Table — Starting Data
slides.caption: Revenue is not a stored column — it must be calculated per row as Quantity × Unit Price

slides.title: The Expression
slides.code:
Total Revenue =
SUMX(
    Orders,
    Orders[Quantity] * Orders[Unit Price]
)
slides.annotation: Orders[Quantity] * Orders[Unit Price] is evaluated in row context — DAX enters each row of Orders and computes the product before moving to the next row.

slides.title: Row-by-Row Evaluation
slides.caption: SUMX processes each row individually, then aggregates

slides.title: SUMX vs SUM — When to Use Each
bullets: SUM(column) — aggregates a single existing column. No expression, no row logic.
SUMX(table, expression) — needed when the value to sum must be CALCULATED per row first.
Use SUM when the column you need is already in the table.
Use SUMX when you need row-level math first (e.g., Price × Qty, Discount × Amount).
slides.keyPoint: If Revenue is not stored as a column, SUM cannot compute it. SUMX is required because it creates the per-row result before aggregating.
slides.warning: SUMX on a large table can be slow if the expression is complex. For simple column sums, always prefer SUM over SUMX(Table, Column).
